snippet.title: I DREAMED ABOUT THESE…
snippet.description: Here is how I made them!  Cannoli Donuts  Dough 1 cup warm milk 3 tbs sugar 1 packet instant yeast 1/4 cup butter, melted 4 large egg yolks 1 tsp vanilla extract 3 cups bread flour Oil, for frying Cannoli Cream 1 1/2 cups heavy cream 1/2 cup ricotta 1 tsp vanilla extract 1/4 cup powdered sugar Mini chocolate chips For Finishing Powdered sugar, for coating Instructions In a large bowl, combine the warm milk, sugar, yeast, melted butter, egg yolks, and vanilla. Add the bread flour and mix until a dough forms. Knead until smooth and elastic, then cover and let rise for 1 hour or until doubled in size. Roll out the dough and cut into donut shapes. Place on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise for another 30 minutes. Heat oil to 350 and fry the donuts until golden brown on both sides. Remove and place on a wire rack to cool. For the cannoli cream, mix the heavy cream until soft peaks form. Add the ricotta, vanilla, and powdered sugar and continue mixing until light and fluffy. Fold in the mini chocolate chips. Once the donuts have cooled, dip them in powdered sugar, then fill generously with the cannoli cream. Enjoy!

snippet.title: WATCH: Guard shouts at Hegseth's group for laughing at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
snippet.description:
A guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier admonished Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s group for laughing loudly after taking photos at the solemn memorial Wednesday. 

The incident happened following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery. 

Video shows the guard, known as a sentinel, yelling loudly at the group to "maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect" after one of the ladies laughed.

It was not immediately clear who among the group was laughing, or why.

What they're saying:
Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell responded to FOX Local’s request for comment on the incident with the following statement:

"The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored—and will always honor—the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe. While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum."
